Abstract and Poster Structure

Use with your mentor to develop a feasible study. This is an educational planning aid, not an approved IRB protocol or a substitute for current institutional templates.

Click a shaded field to replace its prompt. Edits stay in this page only and reset on refresh. Use Print / Save as PDF to retain your work. Use nonconfidential planning text.

· Project Examples Library

Title and Author Credit

[Accurate study title, authors, affiliations, and approved acknowledgments. Identify the actual design.]

Background and Objective

[Brief problem and gap, followed by the prespecified question or hypothesis.]

Methods

[Setting/dates; eligibility; design; exposure/intervention and comparison; primary outcome; sample rationale; analysis; missing-data handling; applicable review/approval.]

Results

[Actual analyzed denominators, participant flow, outcome estimates and uncertainty. Distinguish prespecified from exploratory analyses. Do not invent results to fill this worksheet.]

Conclusion and Limits

[State what the design and estimates support. Explain important uncertainty and limitations. Do not convert an observational association into a causal claim or an imprecise null result into proof of equivalence.]

Poster Layout

[Use the same objective-methods-results-conclusion chain. Select a small number of readable figures/tables with denominators, units, legends, and uncertainty.]

Dissemination Check

[Confirm meeting/journal requirements, all-author review, permissions, disclosures, and absence of participant identifiers. Record whether this is a draft, presented abstract/poster, or published paper.]
